label: py_sincerities_fast
method: numba compilation of round3/py_sincerities (SINCERITIES / SINCERITIES_PLUS / run_sincerities) - zero semantic change, bit-exact by construction and by audit
impl_route: round3/py_sincerities copied verbatim with three compilation/scheduling-only accelerations: (1) two-sample KS D statistic reimplemented as a numba @njit(cache=True) kernel replicating scipy 1.16 ks_2samp(method='auto').statistic statement-by-statement INCLUDING the unconditional h/lcm re-rounding of the statistic (h = int(round(d*lcm)), d = h*1.0/lcm, lcm = n1/gcd*n2) that round3 inherits from scipy; distance-matrix built by one kernel call per adjacent time-point pair (time-point aggregation); (2) coordinate descent: same _cd_path_core as round3, @njit(cache=True, fastmath=False); (3) SINCERITIES main path restructured into three phases - serial numpy preprocessing exactly as round3 (_standardize_train/_lambda_path per (gene,alpha), per-fold standardization cached by identity since it is deterministic numpy), prange batch over flattened (gene, alpha, fit) tasks each executing the identical njit _cd_path on the identical input arrays, serial numpy finalization exactly as round3 (Braw = B/sd, intercept mu@Braw, held-out prediction X_in[~tr]@Bk+ak via the same BLAS calls, sse/cvm/argmin/alpha-selection/min_idx=max(which(cv_err==min))); parallelism changes task completion order only - genes are dataflow-independent and the main path has no RNG. SINCERITIES_PLUS keeps the round3 structure with the numba KS matrix; pcor/cmtest2/final_ranked_predictions/run_sincerities orchestration verbatim
parity_mode: bit_exact vs round3/py_sincerities on the SAME input (np.array_equal on adj_matrix and DISTANCE_matrix, element equality on final_table Interaction/source/target/edges/order): selfcheck on exp_smoke[:300] x 6 stage-ranked time points; plus kernel-level bit-exact audits (KS vs scipy 1500/600 cases incl tie-heavy/identical/asymp-size; fused LOOCV vs round3 _cv_glmnet_nn_loocv; parallel vs serial; noDIAG=1 / method=3 / SINCERITIES_PLUS branches)
entry_point: run_sincerities(exp_mat, col_data, distance=1, method=1, noDIAG=0, SIGN=1, CV_nfolds=5, seed=0, nlambda=100, parallel=True) -> dict(adj_matrix, final_table, DISTANCE_matrix, genes); parallel=False forces the serial per-task path (same bits)
semantics_implemented: ALL round3 semantics preserved verbatim (see round3 MANIFEST): distribution-distance matrix (KS default; cmtest2/mean-diff paths unchanged in python; distance=3 AD still NotImplementedError), dt normalization, non-negative elastic-net CD on the exact glmnet objective with glmnet lambda-path heuristics, LOOCV with foldid=1:n and grouped=FALSE pooled mean, alpha grids per method, tie rule max(which(...)), noDIAG exclude-expansion, spearman-pcor sign step (ginv/solve branches), SINCERITIES_PLUS seeded cvFolds analogue + lambda.min/1se + final refit, adj/max normalization, final_ranked_predictions column-major flatten + labels + stable descending sort

KS kernel replicates scipy INCLUDING the statistic h/lcm re-rounding (empirically established: scipy applies it unconditionally, exact-vs-asymp only changes the p-value path) - without this round3 outputs are NOT bit-reproducible

execution-order note (the only intentional difference from round3): (gene, alpha, fit) CD tasks execute in a prange pool instead of round3's nested serial loops; per-task floating-point sequences are identical (same jit'd CD, same precomputed arrays), no cross-task dataflow, no RNG in the main path -> outputs bit-identical (verified)
gene_block parameter (default auto: cap Bbuf at ~4e8 bytes) controls batching granularity for memory; has no effect on results

performance.input: exp_smoke.iloc[:300] (300 genes x 154 cells), time = stage first-appearance rank (AEC=1, HEC=2, T1=3, T2=4, FL=5, Adult=6) -> T=6 SINCERITIES main path, 1500 CD path fits (300 genes x (1 full + 4 LOOCV folds) x 100 lambdas)
performance.verdict: TARGET <= 20s NOT MET on the build workstation (13th Gen Intel i9-13900KF, 8P+16E hybrid cores, 32 hw threads): the measured prange parallel ceiling of this CD workload on this CPU is 18.4x (controlled 300-task batch), and the pipeline runs at that ceiling (CD ~25s of the ~27.4s total; phases KS/pcor/prep/finalize < 2s combined). Closing the remaining ~7s would require changing round3's pinned convergence semantics (tol=1e-10 max|dbeta|, max_sweeps=10000 - R glmnet's Fortran converges on a much looser fractional-deviance 1e-7 criterion, which is why the 14.8s R baseline is faster despite single-core) or relaxing bit-exactness (fastmath/SIMD restructuring - a cross-task interleaved SIMD kernel was prototyped and rejected: 6x SLOWER due to idle-lane work and not bit-exact). On a >20-physical-core machine the wall time scales down with the pool (thread ceiling is the binding constraint).

numba_compatibility_findings: scipy.stats.ks_2samp is NOT njit-able (python dispatch objects) -> hand-written binary-search replication of its statistic path (as the task anticipated); numba's np.searchsorted side='right' support was avoided altogether with an explicit binary search

njit kernels may only call OTHER DISPATCHERS in nopython mode - references to undecorated core functions (_ks2_d_core/_cd_path_core inside _ks_matrix_rows_core/_cd_batch_core) raise Untyped global name TypingError; fixed by referencing the jit'd names
prange is the loop iterator itself: 'for i in range(prange(n))' fails typing with 'No implementation of function range(range_state_int64)'; must be 'for i in prange(n)'
njit functions cannot take lists of arrays as arguments (reflected-list limitation) - batch buffers are packed into single N-dimensional arrays
cache=True persists compiled kernels to the module __pycache__ (first import pays ~2s compile; warm imports load from disk)

the shared IPython kernel caches modules across runs: after editing a module under audit, pop it from sys.modules before re-importing or the old bytecode executes with the new source shown in tracebacks (bit us repeatedly during selfcheck development)
uncertainties: INHERITED from round3 MANIFEST (unchanged): kSamples AD not ported (distance=3); CD-vs-glmnet-Fortran solver deviation class (this candidate is bit-exact vs round3, hence inherits round3's rank_port posture vs R); lambda-path ULP effects; CVFOLDS RNG seedability; pcor ginv branch sensitivity; ORDER stability; method=4 headless refusal.

KS KERNEL SCOPE: the numba kernel reproduces scipy's statistic for real-valued inputs without NaN; NaN inputs (absent in this pipeline) would sort differently - round3/scipy would also be undefined there.

SCIPY VERSION PIN: the replicated statistic path (incl. the h/lcm re-rounding) was verified against scipy 1.16.3; a future scipy that changes the statistic path would break bit-equality with THAT scipy but not with round3 run on the same 1.16.3 environment.

PARALLEL DETERMINISM: prange scheduling is workqueue-based; task set and per-task arithmetic are fixed -> outputs deterministic across runs and thread counts (verified parallel==serial and across repeated runs).
build_cmd: no build step; smoke: python smoke_test.py; selfcheck timing: python selfcheck/run_timing.py
smoke_details: 10/10 PASS (smoke_test.py): U1 KS kernel == scipy statistic bit-exact 600/600 (tie-heavy ints, continuous, identical samples, all-constant, binary, n1*n2>10000 asymp path); U2 KS distance matrix bit-exact vs round3 on the real 300-gene input; U2 fused LOOCV == round3 serial (lambdas vector, cvm curve, lambda.min value, beta@imin) 6/6 bit-exact; U3 SINCERITIES(40 real genes) adj/lambda/alpha bit-exact and parallel==serial bit-exact; U4 noDIAG=1 / method=3 lasso / SINCERITIES_PLUS(T=4, seeded) all bit-exact vs round3; U5 synthetic 100-gene full pipeline 1.1s finite/normalized/10000-row ranked table. SELF-CHECK (selfcheck/): round3 python 525.9s vs numba warm ~27.4s, adj_matrix + DISTANCE_matrix + final_table bit-identical (np.array_equal), outputs of both versions stored for audit.
